newsitem.title: USA: COTTON - Prices seen sharply lower on USDA estimate.
newsitem.headline: COTTON - Prices seen sharply lower on USDA estimate.

text.p: NYCE cotton prices are likely to fall sharply, possibly the 3.00-cent daily limit, on the U.S. Department of Agriculture's October supply and demand report, industry sources said.
While the USDA raised it's estimate for the crop only slightly, it hiked its estimate for ending stocks to 4.5 million bales compared with 3.6 million bales in September.
The USDA put the 1996/97 crop at 18.189 million 480-lb bales compared with 17.9 million bales, and lowered imports to 5.8 million bales from 6.2 million bales in September.
"We're talking about the possiblility for new contract lows," said David Brandon Jr, an anlayst with Smith Barney.
"This report is not neutral but decisively bearish," said Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc.

She said the most-active December contract could find support at key 74.00 cents a lb, "but it will be easier to take that out based on report. A close below that level would decididely change the complexion of the market," Johnson said.
Meanwhile, an unchanged import figure could also weigh on the market. Despite a continued stream of foreign cotton flowing into U.S. ports, the USDA left its estimate unchanged at 500,000 bales.

"We know we will have to increase imports at some point, which will lead to an even higher ending stock figure," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "Flies came into my mouth this morning when I saw the import figure unchanged."
Brandon said Thursday's weekly import number of only 13,438 bales, the lowest weekly figure since May 19, may have prompted the USDA to keep imports flat.
But he agreed that the USDA will have to eventually raise its import forecast.
Market sources said world estimates were also negative for prices, as the USDA raised total production by 1.2 million bales.
"Today should be a bearish fun-fest," Brandon said. "This market could trade with a six in front."
